analysis.title: Weekly power brief #85: Dems sweep – Panic ensues: What the US midterm results mean for Power and resources
key_insights: Democrats won majorities in both the US House and Senate, plus down-ballot gains including the Texas governorship. On 4 November the market split: financials, health care and hyperscalers rallied while data center infrastructure names sold off.

Investors cut positions in power producers and electrical equipment suppliers on fears that tighter federal oversight, state-level moratoria, slower permitting and grid interconnection opposition will delay AI data center spending.

UBS argues the opposite of the pull-forward view held by some market participants. Regulation and grid constraints are expected to smooth and lengthen the AI infrastructure cycle into the late 2020s and 2030s rather than destroy demand.

The Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on an immediate pause on new speculative data center construction, ending tax abatements and strict limits on water and power use. Governor Abbott and state regulators had already begun project reviews to prevent residential rate increases.

Ohio municipalities put data center development on the ballot, including limits or temporary moratoria on projects above a set power or water use. UBS expects these rules to filter which developers and hyperscalers finish projects, not to stop compute demand.

Equipment backlogs for power transformers, switchgear, gas turbines and backup generation run several years, with order books carrying onerous cancellation terms. UBS says earnings of tier-one suppliers are insulated from near-term permitting pauses.

UBS models a realistic buildout of about 90 GW by 2030 against a headline pipeline of about 400 GW in proposed data center power requests, and expects its estimate to prove conservative. It says the pipeline contains duplicate interconnection requests and speculative projects.

Portfolio companies book orders only after permits, a binding utility interconnection agreement and a fixed delivery schedule with non-refundable milestone payments. UBS says tighter oversight may shrink the paper backlog but should not threaten commercialized orders.

Many holdings now trade at or below pre-AI-narrative valuations. UBS says the market is assigning near-zero residual value to future AI-driven power demand and calls the sell-off an attractive risk-adjusted entry point, with conviction in the Power and resources theme still high.

Clean energy developers and regulated utilities rallied on expectations of renewed federal incentives or clean power mandates and lower interest rates. The Power and resources strategy gained in the week ending 30 October and beat the MSCI ACWI Index, led by equipment, facilitators and utilities.
The report notes that from 1 November 2026 UBS CIO no longer rates equities as Most Preferred or Least Preferred and instead labels stocks as CIO Selected, which is a designation and not a rating.

sector_views.sector: AI power and electrical infrastructure (IPPs and electrical equipment)
sector_views.rationale: Backlogs, committed projects and well-capitalized hyperscaler customers support the buildout, and valuations after the sell-off sit near pre-boom levels. Regulation is expected to extend the cycle, not end it.
Rallied on 4 November on expected federal incentives and lower rates. The report describes the move without giving a separate directional call.

earnings_insights: Equipment backlogs for power transformers, switchgear, gas turbines and backup generation stretch several years, and order books carry onerous cancellation terms, so UBS sees tier-one industrial supplier earnings growth as insulated from near-term permitting pauses (UBS view, not a reported figure).
UBS expects additional power supply agreements to be announced in 4Q26 and 1Q27 despite the policy uncertainty (forecast).

Portfolio companies book orders into backlog only after environmental permits, a binding utility interconnection agreement and a fixed delivery schedule with non-refundable milestone payments, so a reduction would hit paper backlog first.

trade_ideas.description: Buy the post-election sell-off in AI power and electrical equipment names held in the UBS Power and resources selection list, including Vistra, Constellation Energy, Eaton, nVent Electric and Forgent
trade_ideas.rationale: Tighter oversight should extend rather than derail the AI infrastructure cycle, and valuations already price in significant pessimism.
trade_ideas.risk: Regulatory uncertainty, slower permitting and grid constraints could delay data center expansion, and no single catalyst will instantly erase market skepticism.

risk_factors: Tighter federal oversight, state-level moratoria and grassroots opposition to data center grid interconnection could slow AI infrastructure spending.
Texas policy reversal toward pausing speculative data center builds, ending tax abatements and limiting water and power use.
Local limits and moratoria in Ohio on projects above set power or water thresholds.
Development may need time to migrate to friendlier jurisdictions, and some pipeline requests are duplicated across regions.
Sentiment may take time to recover and there is no single catalyst to remove skepticism about the buildout.
Company-specific risks include fading data center capex enthusiasm (Eaton), a slowdown in electrical equipment demand (Forgent), and federal regulation and plant operations (Vistra).
vol_and_positioning: Investors are derisking data center infrastructure positions after the election, with Vistra's 14% drop its worst single day in nearly two years.
The report describes a continued rotation out of AI-related stocks in recent days.
A sharp bifurcation on 4 November: financials, health care and hyperscalers rallied while power producers and electrical equipment makers sold off.
Many holdings trade near or below their valuations from before the AI data center narrative took hold.
geopolitical: US midterm elections gave Democrats majorities in the House and Senate, raising the prospect of a more restrictive federal stance on AI infrastructure.
Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governorship, the first Democratic gubernatorial victory in Texas since 1990, on a platform of pausing speculative data center construction.
Ohio municipalities placed data center limits and temporary moratoria on the ballot.
A further escalation of US-China tensions is named as a risk for Zhongji Innolight.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS argues regulatory rigor, localized reviews and grid constraints will smooth and lengthen the cycle into the late 2020s and 2030s. Multi-year backlogs, committed customer investment and valuations near pre-boom levels support the view.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors fear tighter federal oversight, state moratoria and grassroots opposition to interconnection will derail AI infrastructure spending, as reflected in the Vistra (-14%) and Forgent (-17%) declines.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees constraints elongating demand, with projects migrating to welcoming rural jurisdictions and hyperscalers paying concessions.
tension_points.bear_case: Some market participants argue political friction will pull peak infrastructure demand forward as developers rush projects before tighter rules take effect.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tighter oversight will extend rather than derail the AI infrastructure cycle, and the sell-off improves risk-reward.
theme_stances.evidence: Our conviction in the Power and resources opportunity remains high.

theme_stances.key_argument: Large loads must self-fund and prove grid reliability, which UBS believes hyperscalers are willing to do.
theme_stances.evidence: Large loads must pay their own way, bring their own power
